Tell me in four or five sentences why the sky is blue.

The sky looks blue because sunlight contains every color, and as it enters the atmosphere, air molecules scatter the shorter wavelengths much more strongly than the longer ones. Blue light has a shorter wavelength than red, so it gets bounced around in all directions and reaches your eyes from every part of the sky. Red and orange light mostly pass straight through, which is why direct sunlight looks yellowish-white and sunsets look red. This scattering process is called Rayleigh scattering, and it depends steeply on wavelength, roughly the inverse fourth power. Violet light scatters even more than blue, but the sun emits less of it and our eyes are less sensitive to it, so the sky appears blue.
